column1: # NEXUS — assertions that have been SHOWN able to fail, one row per witnessed arm.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The gate has 216 assertions; D102 measured that the ledgers name somewhere between 53
# and 57 of them depending on how the text is matched, and that a mention is only an upper bound on being
# witnessed. What has never existed is a machine-readable record of the stronger claim — "this row was seen red"
# — because every plant this lane has run lives in a temp-dir harness and a paragraph of prose. A count of
# witnesses that cannot be recomputed is a story, so this is the record, and scripts/check_falsifier_registry.mjs
# checks it against the gate's own list of rows rather than against anyone's memory.
# RULES, enforced by the checker:
#   * `check` must be an assertion the gate actually files, read back from `qc` in a loaded database. The
#     polymorphic sweeps build their names at run time, so a name here that is not in qc is a transcription.
#   * `witness` is an artifact that still exists or a commit that still resolves — not a description.
#   * One row per (check, arm). A check witnessed by three arms is three rows; the claim being recorded is
#     per-arm, and collapsing arms is how a number starts meaning less than it says.
